In doing research for new content and just through general observation over the last couple of years I've noticed that every mass shooting or act of violence seems to get labeled as a false flag almost right off the bat. It's the first thing that is mentioned in the conspiracy circles after pretty much any such event. It seems logical, given that these types of attacks have been proven to take place, that some of them inevitably are but some of them are bound to just be genuinely unstable people who finally snap or acts of terrorism carried out by extremist groups, etc. My question is: how many of these events are actually false flags, and what steps can we take to verify or help substantiate those claims? Inconsistencies in the story can point to something being awry, but with the media feeding frenzy and internet vigilantism those can also simply be chocked up to poor journalism. In the case of Sandy Hook there was some pretty compelling evidence surrounding the body language and general behavior of the victim's families and those said to have examined the bodies. What other signs can we point to to help identify potential false flags, and in what way, if any, can we rule out such an event from being one?

It is my hope with this community that we can be more than just a dumping ground for conspiracy theories, and engage in discussion and critical thinking about these kinds of events to help separate the signal from the noise.

I definitely agree with the accessibility argument. In the previous bubble a lot of people became fans, and then when they became fans they got disillusioned with how the anime industry was handling the west. To support the industry we had to sometimes wait years to purchase something after it aired in Japan. It was easier just to pirate. It actually became engrained in fan culture that buying was a bad thing to do. You were getting ripped off, or played for a sucker.

Today that school of thought still exists, but new fans are also able to support the anime industry through streaming. Additionally we can buy BDs about the same time as our Japanese counterparts. The only thing western fans lag in right now really is OVAs and movies.

I hope someone steps up to the plate to fix this.
